findings.description: The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so the database storage and its snapshots are stored unencrypted with no customer-managed KMS key.
publicly_accessible = true assigns the RDS MySQL instance a public IP and DNS name, exposing the database service to the internet rather than keeping it in a private network layer.
The master username is the default 'admin', a predictable administrative account name that eases credential-guessing attacks against an internet-reachable database.
The master password is supplied via var.password and is also interpolated into EC2 user data; the value is stored in plaintext in Terraform state and is not sourced from a secrets manager.
No enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports (audit, error, general, slowquery) are configured, so database access and security-relevant events are not retained for audit.

The inline role policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*", giving the EC2 instance near-administrative control over all storage, compute and database resources in the account — a direct privilege escalation and data exfiltration path if the instance is compromised.
The egress rule allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the RDS security group, providing an unrestricted data exfiltration and command-and-control channel.

The EC2 user_data script embeds the database password (var.password) and username in cleartext; user data is readable by anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute and via the instance metadata service from within the instance.

No metadata_options block sets http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled and an SSRF in the hosted PHP app could retrieve the instance role's credentials, which carry near-admin permissions.
No root_block_device/ebs encryption is specified, so the instance volumes containing the credentials file (/var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc) may be stored unencrypted.
The instance is launched in a web subnet and exposes a public DNS name serving an unauthenticated HTTP-only PHP page, so application traffic including form data traverses the network unencrypted.

The RDS security group is created without inline rules and combined with publicly_accessible = true; any broadening of the attached rules directly exposes MySQL to the internet. It also lacks a description and relies on default egress-allow behaviour before the explicit rules apply.
